The installer should be able to copy the static application, but its global /proc scan fails before doing so. A conforming installer can skip database-inactivity inspection when the database and its journals are all absent while retaining conservative protection for an existing database. unresolved.suggested_fix: Skip the inactivity scan for a genuinely absent database and journals, or use a database-scoped ownership/locking mechanism; preserve refusal when an existing database may be active and add the unrelated-process fresh-install control.

Deliberate fixture changes are explicit: synthetic app and local RewardKit CLI stub only; frozen test.sh, score.py and scoring policy are unchanged. The stub values/reward are not configured judge, Oracle, target-model, portal or full-workload evidence. Full configured measurements remain absent; this verdict rests on the concrete lifecycle execution, not on those missing measurements.
unresolved.counterexample: Broken alternative: an otherwise convincing app keeps newly written records only in memory and handles SIGTERM without exiting. The helper reports a successful restart even though the same PID and memory survived, so hro_restart and hro_change_retry_restart can appear satisfied without actual persistence. The PID/EADDRINUSE mechanism is reproduced; no actual model award is claimed. Conforming alternative: an otherwise fully durable implementation uses an ordinary 30-second graceful shutdown, which the public integration contract does not forbid. The reproduced helper proceeds after five seconds, fails to bind its replacement, and reports success against the still-running old process. When that scheduled shutdown completes, later browser checks can lose the app. Source plus the observed retained PID establish this failure path; a full configured false-negative score was not measured. An app that leaves its HTTP server alive after SIGTERM can also hold the outer cleanup wait indefinitely, regardless of product correctness.
unresolved.suggested_fix: Escalate to the shared-template owner for an authorized canonical lifecycle fix: ensure reward before cleanup, bound termination and escalate to SIGKILL, require the old process group to be gone before restart, and verify the replacement is alive before reporting success; then freeze a new candidate and rerun the matched controls. Preserve the current task/template bytes and scoring policy until that authorized shared change.

G1 (P1): ordinary computed-request claims have no explicit scored observation. Public environment/instructions/hireops_rules.md:363-367 and385-386 require stored composition/settlement to override request claims. The functional prompt:37 mentions session authority, and:45 says not to invent optional claim keys, but prescribes no ordinary approval/revision/rescission replay that changes an actually observed computed monetary claim. Functional hro_claw at judge.toml:587 checks the expected normal UI clawback; role/stale/concurrency criteria test different properties. The explicit saved-intent tamper protocol at functional/prompt.md:59 is only coordinated B3. A normal request containing a browser-computed clawback can therefore be trusted by the server and still meet every ordinary arithmetic/permission/refusal scenario. This is a missing observable for the ordinary stored-fact authority promise, not a demand for a private field name.

G2 (P1): financial existence/readback can substitute for required on-screen financial detail. Public hireops_rules.md:392-407 explicitly requires figures in ordinary product views, including the equity vesting schedule, signing remittance and referral halves/cliff. Functional/prompt.md:3 and13 permit ordinary response data as evidence. hro_grant at functional/judge.toml:479 requires that a grant 'contains' its units/start/schedule; hro_signing:488 and hro_referral_creation:506 similarly inspect records without requiring their display. The hro_referral_clock description:641 checks the cliff result, while P8 says to read dates/splits without closing the response-only alternative. Visual/prompt.md:10 is craft review of whatever harmless surfaces are available, and its criteria do not own missing financial fields. Thus a usable-looking Equity page can omit the required vesting schedule and a Referrals page can omit halves/cliff while their normal authenticated payload contains everything the financial checks read. Explicitly visible intrinsic/annual/run-rate rows do not cover those separate displays.

G3 (P2): refusal explanations are not fully mapped. instruction.md:7 requires 'Explain these failures clearly'. Polish/judge.toml:23 owns revision retained input/recovery and expressly excludes the budget/shortfall wording; it does not require any displayed failure explanation. Polish/judge.toml:41 similarly owns stale-change retained terms/recovery without a clear displayed explanation bar. In contrast rescission:32 expressly requires a visible failure and uncertain commit:50 expressly requires UI uncertainty/failure. A revision or stale commit can fail silently in the UI, retain inputs, and later correct successfully while satisfying the two relevant scored descriptions. No exact amounts or copy should be mandated, but an understandable explanation of the failed operation is asked for.

G4 (P2): change-set preparation refusal retention is ungraded. instruction.md:7 says to keep entered change-set terms after refusal. Polish/judge.toml:41 and polish/prompt.md:14 exercise only refusal of a previously saved preview at commit time. A form that preserves values after stale commit but clears selections/destinations/terms after a rejected prepare satisfies those criteria and violates the stated retained-entry requirement. This is a distinct prepare-stage recovery path, not an additional test of an arbitrary layout.

Conforming alternative considered: an app with no client-supplied computed claims, generated record IDs, dollar-valued requests, details in expandable panels, standard native validation, and equivalent date formatting must remain valid. Any repair should inspect only observed claim fields, accept omission/rejection of extraneous claims, and check rendered facts/clear failure meaning without prescribing routes, field names, schemas or exact text. Existing wording already correctly permits generated IDs, omitted optional history, varied layouts and simple independent controls.
